title: Constraint: 6 × 6 Sudoku
constraints: Fill a 6 × 6 grid with 1 … 6 so that every row, every column and every 2 × 3 box (2 rows × 3 columns) contains each digit exactly once.
Clues: `g[0][0] = 1` and `g[5][5] = 6`. Successive calls should produce different grids.
Runs on Verilator with the z3 solver (`sudo pacman -S z3`).
hints: "Each digit exactly once" in a group of six is the same as "all six are different".
Two cells conflict when they share a row, a column, or a box (`i/2 == k/2 && j/3 == l/3`). One pairwise constraint covers all three.

`unique {…}` would be elegant, but Verilator only supports it on 1-D arrays (watch the Compile stage for warnings). The classic 9 × 9 version is also out of reach of Verilator's solver interface in reasonable time.

examples.check: rows, columns and 2x3 boxes contain each value once
examples.title: valid grid
examples.expected: every row, column and box is a permutation of 1…6
